comparison: Strong agreement on PRMT1-high cells driving leukemogenesis (C2, C3, C57-C59, C67). Both evaluations find this a key, well-supported discovery. Peer review additionally includes C60-C61 (phenotypic observations) and C139 (LSC interpretation) which OpenEval addresses separately in R14 and R24.

Complete agreement on MS023 therapeutic efficacy (C4, C69-C73, C76, C78-C79). Both evaluations find the data convincing with significant therapeutic implications. Peer review includes C75 which OpenEval does not explicitly mention.

Strong agreement on enhanced glycolysis findings (C5, C7-C8, C80-C88, C15). Both describe this as conceptually novel and well-supported. Peer review additionally includes C6 (mitochondrial respiration), C110, C112 (glucose dependence) which OpenEval addresses separately in R4 and R7.

Strong agreement on CPT1A downregulation and lipid accumulation (C9-C10, C124-C127, C16, C137). Both find these claims well-supported. Peer review additionally includes C105-C107 (beta-oxidation impairment) and C128-C129 (etomoxir/orlistat sensitivity) which OpenEval addresses separately in R9 and R11.

Strong agreement on 2-DG therapeutic efficacy and glucose dependence (C12, C114-C117). Both find the in vivo data convincing. Peer review additionally includes C13 (differentiation) and C111-C113 (glucose dependence details) which OpenEval addresses separately in R7 and R15.

Agreement on CPT1A rescue experiments and short-chain fatty acid utilization (C132-C133, C138). Both find this strengthens mechanistic links. Peer review additionally includes C14 and C134-C136 which OpenEval addresses separately in R10 and R16.

Agreement on paradoxical mitochondrial findings (C89-C90, C92-C93, C97, C167-C168). Both find the increased mitochondrial biogenesis despite reduced respiration conceptually novel. Peer review additionally includes C94-C96, C98-C99, C169 (ROS and redox state) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12, R13, and R22.
Agreement on metabolomic analysis quality and comprehensiveness (C101-C104, C108-C109). Both evaluations find the metabolomic data robust and well-supported, with no methodological concerns raised.

Partial overlap on glucose dependence claims (C110-C113). OpenEval finds these well-supported by multiple assays. Peer review groups these with broader 2-DG therapeutic findings (R5) rather than treating glucose dependence separately.

Partial overlap on CPT1A variant experiments (C134-C136). OpenEval finds the data supportive but notes mechanism could be explored further. Peer review groups this with broader CPT1A rescue findings, emphasizing it strengthens mechanistic links.

Partial overlap on etomoxir/orlistat sensitivity (C128-C129). OpenEval finds this provides additional evidence for altered fatty acid metabolism. Peer review groups this with broader fatty acid oxidation findings rather than treating it separately.

Partial overlap on ROS measurements (C94-C96). OpenEval finds the cytoplasmic ROS inference reasonable. Peer review groups this with broader mitochondrial findings, noting the intriguing nature of alternative energy source utilization.

Partial overlap on GSH/NADPH redox state (C98-C99). OpenEval finds C100 (anabolism promotion) somewhat speculative. Peer review groups redox findings with mitochondrial data and does not specifically critique the anabolism interpretation.

Agreement on phenotypic observations and AMKL model validity (C60-C61, C64-C65, C68). Both evaluations accept these as supporting evidence that the model resembles human disease, with no methodological concerns raised.

Agreement on fusion protein stability control (C63). Both evaluations accept this as important supporting data showing PRMT1 acts through metabolic rather than fusion protein mechanisms. No concerns raised.

Agreement on LSC and therapeutic implications (C140-C143). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct LSC testing. Peer review accepts these as reasonable inferences without specific critique, implicitly supporting the interpretations.

Partial overlap on epigenetic speculation (C163-C164). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative proposals not directly tested. Peer review accepts these as reasonable hypotheses for future directions without critique.

Partial overlap on mitochondrial function interpretation (C166, C174). OpenEval finds conclusions reasonable but somewhat speculative. Peer review accepts these interpretations without specific critique as part of broader discussion implications.
Partial overlap on lipid-ROS causality (C173). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the causal relationship is not directly tested. Peer review accepts this as reasonable speculation without critique.

Partial overlap on broader applicability (C177). OpenEval finds this reasonable speculation based on conservation. Peer review accepts this as part of discussion implications without specific evaluation.

Divergence on differentiation claim (C13). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to missing figure data. Peer review groups this with 2-DG therapeutic findings and describes it as demonstrating therapeutic potential without expressing uncertainty.

Divergence on CPT1A rescue in glucose-free conditions (C14). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to missing specific data. Peer review groups this with CPT1A rescue experiments and finds it strengthens mechanistic links without expressing uncertainty.

OpenEval identifies unpublished RBM15 target data and platelet/megakaryocyte CPT1A expression (C151-C152, C176) as UNCERTAIN due to unavailable data. Peer review does not specifically address these claims.

OpenEval finds alternative carbon source utilization and short-chain fatty acid metabolism (C153-C154, C156) well-supported. Peer review does not separately evaluate these specific mechanistic details.
OpenEval finds LDHA phosphorylation mechanism (C157-C159) well-supported as linking PRMT1 to glycolysis. Peer review does not separately evaluate this specific mechanistic detail.

Minimal overlap on anabolism interpretation (C100). OpenEval groups this with GSH/NADPH data and notes it's somewhat speculative. Peer review groups it with LSC interpretations and accepts without specific critique.
Peer review explicitly addresses clinical relevance background claims (C1, C51-C52) as accepted established knowledge. OpenEval does not separately evaluate these background/rationale claims.
